title: How we scaled fast, reliable configuration distribution to thousands of workload containers
read_scope: Complete substantive body from configuration challenge through lessons and future work; diagrams cross-read with prose; no code executed.

practice.trigger: Many workers repeatedly read small, slowly changing tenant configuration.
practice.problem: Worker reads, connections, cold caches and missing invalidations couple serving to the central configuration database.
practice.mechanism: Publish snapshots through object storage and full tenant updates through Kafka; workers serve from local RocksDB; initial snapshot gates readiness and both distribution paths run normally.
practice.limits: Configuration must fit locally and update traffic must stay manageable; stale configuration needs an operation-specific freshness contract; reported fleet results are not guarantees.
practice.counterexample: Direct-database fallback can recreate overload; policy revocations can require stricter freshness than parsing rules.
practice.verification: Check versions and policy effect through snapshot/update overlap, missing notification, deletion, stale replay, each path outage and simultaneous startup.

crosschecks.read_scope: Message Delivery Semantics and Log Compaction guarantees; current docs linked as latest from Kafka 4.1.
crosschecks.finding: External output and consumer position require coordination. Compaction preserves record order but deletion markers have a configured retention horizon.
